question: Before merging, is the documented `update_partial` contract with status/Doctor inspection and a fresh plan an acceptable recovery guarantee for external package and Gateway failures, once exact-head live proof demonstrates those failure paths?
rationale: Tests and CI cannot establish the real package-installer and Gateway mutation outcomes or whether the proposed operator recovery is acceptable for an experimental lifecycle that may leave retained artifacts.

options.title: Require live recovery proof first
options.body: Keep the fail-closed contract, but require redacted exact-head package replacement, Gateway cron retry/convergence, and retained-artifact recovery evidence before merge.

options.title: Accept the limited recovery contract
options.body: Merge with `update_partial` as the supported boundary after explicitly accepting status/Doctor inspection plus fresh replanning as the operator recovery path.

options.title: Pause apply until reconciliation exists
options.body: Defer the mutation stage until it has immutable operation identity and a stronger reconcile/retry workflow for uncertain external effects.

recommendation.title: Require live recovery proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed contract, but require redacted exact-head package replacement, Gateway cron retry/convergence, and retained-artifact recovery evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They previously identified the concrete external-boundary recovery requirement and can route the required lifecycle acceptance decision.
